description.narrative: IFC proposes to provide an unfunded financial guarantee of up to MXN2,125 million (approximately US$115 million equivalent), covering the mezzanine (second-loss) tranche of a reference portfolio of MXN17,000 million (approximately US$920 million equivalent) in performing SME loan exposures originated by BBVA Mexico, S.A. (BBVA Mexico). The transaction is structured as a Significant Risk Transfer (SRT) - Bursatilizacion Sintetica, with the mezzanine tranche sized at 12.5% of the reference portfolio (attachment point: 1.5%; detachment point: 14.0%). The reference portfolio is denominated in Mexican Pesos (MXN)

Project Outcome: Increased Access to Finance for SMEs, including underserved regions and women SMEs. The Project is expected to contribute to the WBG Scorecard Indicator: (12.2) Millions of people and businesses using financial services, of which (%) are women. The Project expands access to finance for SMEs in Mexico, which face an US$186 billion financing gap (16% of GDP) and where 29% of firms report credit constraints. Through regulatory capital relief enabled by the SRT, BBVA Mexico can redeploy released capital to support firm growth, productivity, and employment, while improving capital efficiency without increasing leverage. The Project strengthens the capacity to expand SME lending, particularly to Women SMEs and underserved regions such as the South and Southeast. It also promotes scalable, data-driven lending platforms within regulated banks, with IFC supporting their expansion and replication to improve SME access to finance. Contribution to Market Creation: Increasing Market Resilience The Project forms part of a broader IFC program across LAC aimed at strengthening resilience through innovative capital tools. Demonstration effects may catalyze additional SRT issuances, attract private investors, and enable institutions to free up capital for inclusive credit growth without issuing new equity or Tier II capital, contributing to long-term financial sector resilience.
